 Order

1. This Miscellaneous Second Appeal under Section 71 (6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against the order dated 28.05.2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge, District Morena in MCA No.67/2022, by which the appeal filed by respondents was allowed and the order dated 24.02.2022 passed by the Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate Morena in case No.01/2020/Food Safety, was set aside.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. According to the prosecution case, on 26/07/2019, the house of respondent No.1 was searched by the Food Safety Officer in presence of respondent No.1.
It was found that 153 sealed tins of Kamani crisp refined palm kernel oil were stored.
On inquiry, respondent No.1 informed that the basement of his house was given by him to respondent No.2 on rent, who is in the business of dairy.
Respondent No.1 could not produce the rent note, bills of purchase of the palm oil.
The samples of the palm oil were collected.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 2 MSA-10-2025
The Food Analyst found that they were an adulterant under Section 3(1)(a) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

An FIR,
bearing crime No.478/2019, was also registered at the Police Station Kailaras District Morena for offences under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, against respondents.
A copy of the report of the Food Analyst was served on the respondents and both of them gave it in writing that they do not want to get the samples re-tested from the Referral Laboratory.

In reply to the show cause notice, respondent No.1 had also The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62493681/
1 provided a copy of rent note to show that the basement was given on rent to respondent No. 2 on 10.06.2019 for a period of 11 months.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Adjudicating Authority, after recording evidence, held that the appellants were guilty of violating the provisions of Section 26(2) and their act is punishable under Sections 57(1) and 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and accordingly, imposed a fine of Rs.2,00,000/- each on respondents No.1 and 2 under Section 57 of the FSSA, and a fine of Rs. 2,00,000/- each on them under Section 58 of the FSSA, i.e. total Rs.4 Lac each was imposed on the respondents No.1 & 2.
3.

Being aggrieved by the said order, respondents No.1 and 2 preferred an appeal which was registered as MCA No.67/2022 and, by order dated 28/05/2024, the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge Morena set aside the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority primarily on the ground that the seized palm oil was not examined within a period of 14 days and the Food Analyst had started the testing after 103 days of collection of samples and there is nothing on record to suggest that the Food NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 3 MSA-10-2025 Analyst had informed the competent authority with regard to delay in carrying out the test as required under Section 46(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act and Food Safety Officer did not visit the dairy of respondent No.2 and did not collect any sample from there.

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The entire action was taken by Food Safety Officer merely on suspicion that respondent No.2 must be using the palm oil for the purposes of adulterating milk.
Merely because the Food Analyst had declared the palm oil as an adulterant, it cannot be said that respondent No.2 had stored the aforesaid palm oil with an intention to mix it with milk.

So far as respondent No.1 is concerned, it was held that though the place from where it was recovered was in his possession of respondent No.1, but there is nothing on record to suggest that respondent No.1 was jointly running the business of dairy along with respondent No.2.
4.
This Court on 03.02.2026 had passed the following order :

"It is submitted by counsel for appellant that 153 sealed tins of palm oil were seized from the basement of the house of respondent No.1, and it was the case of respondent No.1 that the said articles were owned by respondent No.2, who is having his milk dairy in Jaura.
It is submitted by counsel for appellant that the appellate tribunal has set aside the order passed by the adjudicating authority on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove that the respondent No.2 was having any dairy in Jaura and no samples were collected from the dairy and the respondent No.1 cannot be punished only for giving the premises on rent to respondent No.2.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the appellate tribunal has lost certain important aspects which are required to be adjudicated.
(i.)
Whether the respondent No.1 had any building permission to construct a basement in his house ?

The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62493681/
2 (ii.)

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If there was any building permission, then whether the said basement could have been let out to the respondent No.2 for storage of huge quantity of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 4 MSA-10-2025 palm oil ?
(iii.) Whether the respondent No.2 was having any dairy in Jaura, as it is submitted by Shri Bahirani that the respondent number No.2 was not having any dairy in Jaura.
Accordingly, respondent No.1 is directed to file the building permission of the house from where the 153 sealed tins of palm oil were recovered.

If the building permission contains the permission to construct a basement, then the respondent No.1 shall also clarify that for what purposes the basement could have been constructed, and whether it could have been used for commercial purposes or not ?

Counsel for respondent No.2 is also directed to make a categorical statement as to whether the respondent No.2 is running any milk dairy in Tehsil Jaura, District Morena, or not, and if not, then whether he is giving his no objection to the action which the local administration can take against the said dairy by sealing the same.
As prayed, list on 05.02.2026 ."

5. In response to the aforesaid order, the respondents have filed a copy of the building permission to show that the Gram Panchayat Antri Janpad Panchayat Kailaras District Morena had granted No Objection Certificate for building construction on 18/02/2015 and the layout plan for the basement,
showroom, first floor and second floor was passed by Gram Panchayat Antri.

entities.text: Gram Panchayat Antri Janpad Panchayat Kailaras District Morena
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 6. Similarly, counsel for State has provided a copy of a licence dated 13.06.2024 issued in favour of respondent No.2 for manufacturing and trading of dairy and milk products.
7. It is fairly conceded by counsel for the State that the palm oil was seized on 26.07.2019 i.e. prior to issuance of the licence.

8. However, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that the appellate Tribunal should have remanded the matter back to the Adjudicating NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 5 MSA-10-2025 Authority because respondent No.2 in his evidence has stated the he does not own any dairy but he only sells packed tins of palm oil.
It is submitted that respondent No.2 has not produced any document to show that he had any business of selling palm oil only.

It is further submitted that appellate Tribunal lost sight of fact that generally basements are to be used for parking purposes and not for any other purposes and under what circumstances, the respondent No.1 stored large quantity of palm oil has also not been explained by him.
On the contrary, he had merely stated that he had let out the basement to respondent No.2 and that the palm oil was of respondent No.2.
However, respondent No.2 did not produce any receipt to show that from whom he had purchased the large quantity of palm oil.
9. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

3 10.

entities.text: State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A large quantity of sealed palm oil tins was seized from the basement of the house of respondent No.1.

It is the case of the State that the Municipal Corporation was already in existence much prior to construction of the building from where the palm oil was seized, but according to respondent Nos.1 and 2, the building permission was obtained from the Panchayat.

The respondents have not filed the copy of the building permission issued by the Gram Panchayat Antri, Janpad Panchayat Kailaras but have merely filed a copy of the layout plan for basement, showroom, first floor and second floor.

Whether the Gram Panchayat had any authority to sanction the layout plan for residential as well as commercial purposes, including basement area or not, is also a serious question which requires adjudication.

Furthermore, from the certificate (Anneuxre R-1), it is clear NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 6 MSA-10-2025 that in fact a No Objection Certificate was issued by the Gram Panchayat and there is nothing from this certificate to show that the Gram Panchayat had any authority to sanction the layout plan.

11. Be that whatever it may be.
12.

For the time being, the aforesaid question does not require any elaborate discussion at this stage,
except by saying that the Gram Panchayat Antri had issued a No Objection Certificate for raising construction of the building, but that cannot be treated as building permission.

13. Furthermore, whether respondent No.2 had purchased the palm oil for commercial purposes or for adulterating milk also requires deeper scrutiny, because when admittedly respondent No.2 has also obtained a licence for running the business of milk/ dairy products.
14. So far as non-testing of samples within 14 days is concerned, there is nothing on record to suggest that packed tin of palm oil would have spoiled after 14 days.
The respondents did not opt for retesting of samples from referral laboratory.
Since the self life of packed palm oil was not over therefore, merely because the samples were not tested within 14 days, the same cannot be a ground to set -aside the proceedings.

15. Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Appellate Tribunal should not have set aside the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority on aforesaid ground as well as on the ground that the respondent No.1 had merely allowed the respondent No.2 to store 153 tins of palm oil in the basement of his house, and there is nothing on record to suggest that respondent No.2 was running any dairy business in Jaura NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 7 MSA-10-2025 District Morena.

16. Adulteration of milk has to be dealt with seriousness and the prosecution should not be thrown away in a light manner because milk is consumed by infants, old age persons, as well as general public.
Therefore, adulteration of milk will adversely affect the health of consumers of all ages and it has to be checked with all firmness.

If the appellate tribunal had some doubt with regard to the merits of the case, then it should have remanded the matter back to the Adjudicating Authority to collect further evidence and then decide the case.
The same was not done by Appellate Tribunal.

4 17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the appellate tribunal after setting aside the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority should have remanded the matter back and accordingly, the order dated 28.05.2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge, District Morena in MCA No.67/2022, so far as it relates to dismissal of prosecution,
is hereby set -aside and the matter is remanded back to the Adjudicating Authority to give a specific finding on the following issues :
(i) Whether the Gram Panchayat Antri had any authority to grant building permission in the year 2015 because this Court has already held that the No Objection Certificate issued by the Gram Panchayat Antri cannot be treated as a building permission?

entities.text: Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent No.1 shall be free to file any other document to show that any building permission was granted by a competent authority by passing a reasoned order.

(ii) Whether the basement could have been used by respondent No.1 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 8 MSA-10-2025 for commercial purposes or not or whether the basement should have been used only for parking purposes ?

(iii) The respondents shall be free to lead evidence by examining the notary along with his notary register to show that the rent note was executed between the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 on the day on which it is shown to have been executed.

(iv) Respondent No.2 shall file the documents to show that he was running a business of sealed tins of palm oil by producing his registration under different statutes as well as business details including the total purchase of palm oil and the sale of the same by producing the income tax return as well as the receipts and the books of accounts.
(v) The appellant shall also be entitled to lead evidence to show that whether respondent No.2 was running any dairy in Jaura District Morena at the relevant time or not?
18. The parties are directed to appear before the Adjudicating Authority on 23rd March 2026 and no fresh notice is required to be issued to any of the parties.
If any party remains absent before the Adjudicating Authority on the said date, the Adjudicating Authority shall be free to proceed in accordance with law.
19. With aforesaid observation, this MSA is finally disposed of.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Aman The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62493681/
